findings.location: N9 section ('five confounds controlled, and η²_surrogate grew from the published 0.37 to 0.405'), Candidate D one-sentence ('give the protocol that removes them, and show that removing them does not shrink but strengthens ... 0.37 → 0.405'), and the executive summary ('the confound set whose removal strengthens the audited effect ... 0.37 to a corrected 0.405')
findings.issue: The report attributes the 0.37→0.405 strengthening to controlling all FIVE confounds, but the query (gospel) and the draft's own N1 say 0.405 is the result of fixing only (i) target scaling + (ii) candidate/oracle protocol, and at least one of the five — (iv) ensemble size K — pushes the OTHER way (at K=2 the ensemble marginal 0.95 EXCEEDS the exact GP's 0.846, which shrinks/reverses the surrogate effect).
findings.evidence: query-offline-mbo-novelty-audit-6d8cd4.md line 63 ('Fixing (i) and (ii) together does NOT cancel: they net UP to eta^2_surr = 0.405') and line 59 ('At K=2 the ensemble marginal (0.95) EXCEEDS the exact GP's (0.846)'); the draft's own N1 correctly scopes it: 'fixing target scaling and the candidate protocol together nets up to 0.405'.
findings.recommendation: In N9, candidate D, and the exec summary, rescope the strengthening claim so 0.405 is explicitly the result of fixing the two measurement/protocol confounds (i)+(ii), not 'removing all five.' Add a clause acknowledging that at least one confound (K) moves the surrogate effect DOWNWARD, so the honest claim is 'the net effect of the correctable scaling/protocol confounds is upward,' not 'de-confounding across the whole taxonomy strengthens the effect.' This is the headline the RECOMMENDED candidate (D) rests on, so the overclaim must not ship.

findings.location: N5 verdict ('the objection is already substantially answered ... an existing architecture-size ablation already answers it') and rejecting-citation #1 ('they answered the finite-width objection with an architecture-size ablation the paper did not run')
findings.issue: The report adopts L/R/W Appendix D.1.2 as having 'already answered' the finite-width objection, but the vault note says D.1.2 is 'partial and confounded, not a clean pre-emption': it only tests a SMALLER net (width 128→50), never a WIDER one, so it does not address the objection's actual prediction (a wider network would smooth the jagged ensemble mean and close the gap); it also confounds width with depth and activation and is not framed by the authors as a width study.
findings.evidence: a-study-of-bayesian-neural-network-surrogates-for-bayesian-optimization-iclr-202 (N5 net verdict): 'PRIOR WORK FOUND, but partial and confounded, not a clean pre-emption ... it does not test whether WIDER-than-128 ensembles close the gap ... A clean, isolated, multi-level width sweep for the DEEP ENSEMBLE specifically ... remains genuinely absent.' The draft itself later concedes the objection is 'answerable only with an experiment the paper does not run,' contradicting 'already answers it.'
findings.recommendation: Qualify the N5 verdict: D.1.2 partially blunts but does not settle the finite-width objection because it only tested a smaller architecture (not the wider one the objection predicts would help) and confounds width/depth/activation; the decisive clean width sweep (K fixed, hidden units swept upward) remains absent from the literature. Reconcile with the report's own closing sentence so the two statements do not contradict.

findings.location: Executive summary, para 5: 'Every reality-check the genre is built on runs the other way [5][6]; that inversion is what no prior paper owns.'
findings.issue: The exec summary cites Recht [6] as an example of an audit that 'runs the other way' (shrinks), but the report's own N9 section concedes Recht's relative-gain slope exceeds 1 — 'an increased advantage over earlier models,' which Recht calls 'the opposite of the standard overfitting scenario' — i.e., a growth result. Citing Recht as a clean shrink in the headline while treating it as a partial growth counter-instance in N9 hands a Recht-aware reviewer an easy inconsistency to exploit.
findings.evidence: interim-report-audit-strengthens-and-n9-integrity: Recht is 'a two-track result — absolute accuracy drops ... but the fitted slope of new-test accuracy vs. original-test accuracy exceeds 1 ... which the authors themselves call the opposite of the standard overfitting scenario'; the report's own N9 flags Recht as a PARTIAL that must be pre-empted.
findings.recommendation: In the exec-summary sentence, drop [6] (Recht) from the '[5][6] runs the other way' citation (Melis [5] alone cleanly supports 'audits shrink'), or add a parenthetical noting Recht is the partial exception whose relative-slope growth the paper pre-empts. Keep the headline consistent with the N9 treatment of Recht.

findings.location: Rejecting-citation #2 (Shahriari as 'The reversal-killer', 'this ~5,900-citation survey rejects it in one sentence') and candidate A caveat ('surrogate-over-acquisition primacy is decade-old doctrine')
findings.issue: The report over-concedes to Shahriari without the scope the vault flags: Shahriari's thesis is about the ONLINE-BO acquisition-FUNCTION heuristic (EI/PI/UCB), whereas the paper's optimizer axis is the numerical search algorithm (gradient ascent / hill-climbing / CMA-ES) in the OFFLINE setting. The report then treats 'optimizer' as equivalent to 'acquisition function' when conceding to Shahriari, but as distinct from it when ruling out Liang (surrogate × acquisition-function grid) and L/R/W as N6 counterexamples — an internal inconsistency that either gives Shahriari too much or lets Liang/L-R-W back in as near-counterexamples.
findings.evidence: interim-report-optimizer-reversal-unearned-and-candidate-a-credit boundary condition: 'It does not extend to online/sequential BO, where Shahriari et al.'s doctrine already governs' and the reframing that A owns 'the first offline-MBO-specific ... falsification of PGS's own motivating premise'; the N6 rule-out table itself distinguishes 'optimizer/search varied' from 'acquisition' (Liang crosses surrogate × acquisition-function; L/R/W fixes MC-EI).
findings.recommendation: Add a scope qualifier to the Shahriari concession: Shahriari governs online BO and the acquisition-FUNCTION-family choice, not the numerical optimizer/search axis in offline MBO, so candidate A retains a genuine offline/optimizer-axis residual rather than being fully pre-empted. Make the optimizer-vs-acquisition-function terminology consistent between the Shahriari concession and the N6 Liang/L-R-W rule-out.

findings.location: N4 verdict ('because the β=0 control kills the σ channel, the paper's viable mechanism relocates from posterior variance to posterior mean smoothness') and candidate C ('the β=0 control shows the gap survives σ removal, so the mechanism cannot be σ-mediated')
findings.issue: The body states the β=0 control 'kills the σ channel' / 'cannot be σ-mediated' as settled, but the terminal section (and the vault) mark the β=0 numbers NOT VERIFIABLE — the query's cited 0.51→0.47 could not be reproduced; an independent recomputation gave 0.504→0.511 (flat-to-slightly-up). The direction (gap survives) is robust, but the strong causal claim is stated inline without the hedge that lives only in the terminal section.
findings.evidence: interim-report-n4-sigma-mechanism-scope-and-ovadia: confidence is 'medium on the causal conclusion itself, because it leans on a β=0 control whose exact numbers I could not fully reconcile'; the draft's own 'What I could not verify' section confirms the magnitude discrepancy.
findings.recommendation: Soften the inline wording near the N4 verdict and in candidate C from 'kills the σ channel'/'cannot be σ-mediated' to 'the gap survives removal of the σ term (direction robust, magnitude unreconciled — see terminal section), which argues against a σ-mediated mechanism.' Cross-reference the NOT-VERIFIABLE caveat at the point of the claim so a reviewer does not read the body as a verified refutation.

findings.location: N1 ('none of them computes a variance decomposition. There is no η² ... anywhere in that literature') and candidate D ('the η² decomposition the genre has never used')
findings.issue: The 'no variance decomposition anywhere' phrasing risks overclaiming variance-decomposition novelty. The report's own N6 concedes Hutter's fANOVA is 'the closest model-class-as-a-variance-decomposed-factor result in existence' (one-way) — so a reviewer could argue variance decomposition of model class already exists, and the true residual is the TWO-WAY crossed ANOVA in the offline-MBO setting, not variance decomposition per se.
findings.evidence: an-efficient-approach-for-assessing-hyperparameter-importance-icml-2014 note (fANOVA decomposes performance variance including model class); draft N6 concedes Hutter as the nearest one-way precedent.
findings.recommendation: Scope the N1/candidate-D novelty claim to the reality-check GENRE specifically (Henderson/Ferrari Dacrema/Musgrave/Lucic/Agarwal use no variance decomposition) and cross-reference that fANOVA (Hutter) already owns one-way variance decomposition of model class, so the residual is the two-way crossed surrogate×optimizer ANOVA in offline MBO — not the use of η²/ANOVA itself.

findings.location: N7 verdict: 'NONE FOUND, "first at all," not merely "first in offline MBO"'
findings.issue: The 'first at all' claim is stated more confidently than the vault's evidence supports. The interim holds only medium confidence on the 'any ML field' scope and explicitly did not search NTK/spectral-bias-adjacent DL theory, robotics/control BO variants, or non-English (esp. swarm/evolutionary-computation) venues where a bidirectional smoothness ablation could sit.
findings.evidence: interim-report-n7-roughening-beyond-offline-mbo: 'Only medium on the word any ML field — I did not exhaustively search spectral-bias/NTK-adjacent deep learning theory ... robotics/control BO variants, or non-English-language venues.'
findings.recommendation: Scope 'first at all' to the BO / GP-regression / kernel-methods literature as indexed by arXiv/OpenAlex/Semantic Scholar as of this sweep, and note the unsearched adjacent regions (NTK/spectral-bias DL theory, non-English DDEA/RBFN venues) rather than asserting an unqualified field-wide first.

findings.location: N8 strategic-value paragraph: 'this finding converts the Design-Bench null from a weakness into a mechanism: if platform variance is of the same order as the cell differences ...'
findings.issue: The report uses platform variance to explain the whole grid-wide Design-Bench null, but the observed variance is confined to ENSEMBLE cells on one task (the exact-GP cell matches to 1.000 and every synthetic cell reproduces to 12 decimals per the query). So platform noise is not a grid-wide floor and cannot by itself explain why GP cells are also mutually indistinguishable — the report presents the reframe without engaging this counter-reading.
findings.evidence: query-offline-mbo-novelty-audit-6d8cd4.md N8 (lines 128-132): only the ensemble cell moves ~0.5 units on TF-Bind-8 while 'the exact-GP cell matches to 1.000 and every synthetic cell reproduces to 12 decimal places cross-platform.'
findings.recommendation: Add a qualifier acknowledging that the platform variance was observed only in ensemble cells (GP/synthetic cells reproduce exactly), so it plausibly explains ensemble-cell instability but is not a grid-wide noise floor; the Design-Bench null is better attributed jointly to low power (Agarwal, N=7) AND ensemble-cell platform noise, not to platform noise alone.
